To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the investigated river system is not affected by the sewage treatment plants in terms of antibiotic residues and antibiotic resistance genes, however antibiotic resistance bacteria can be found downstream of the sewage plants.

the investigated sewage treatment plant effluent was the only significant point source for antibiotic residues (macrolides, sulfonamides and trimethopim) and antibiotic resistant ESKAPE bacteria (including E. coli) in the river.

antibiotic residues, antibiotic resistant genes and antibiotic resistant bacteria can be traced in a river system in a catchment area with no clinical, hospital, and intensive livestock facilities and that antibiotic residues and antibiotic resistance genes are significantly increased after the discharge of sewage treatment plant effluent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of antibiotic resistance genes in a drinking water catchment area.
the investigation of the occurrence of antibiotic residues, resistance genes and antibiotic-resistant bacteria in an aquatic ecosystem.
the investigation of antibiotic residues in drinking water, antibiotic resistant bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes in the environment and their possible transfer to drinking water.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the investigated river is a suitable source for drinking water production, but the results of this study should be interpreted with caution, since the sample period was short and the investigated area is small and no other potential sources for antibiotic resistant bacteria and antibiotic residues were investigated.

antibiotic residues, antibiotic resistant bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes were found in the river system, however, the concentrations of the investigated substances did not pose a threat to human health.

no significant impact of the investigated sewage treatment plants on antibiotic resistance in the river could be found, which was in accordance with the low number of detected antibiotic resistant bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
antibiotic residues and antibiotic resistant bacteria are not a threat to the drinking water reservoir, however, antibiotic resistance genes are present in the investigated rivers.
the investigated drinking water reservoir system was not significantly affected by the discharge of treated sewage effluents in terms of antibiotic residues and antibiotic resistant bacteria.
the investigated drinking water reservoir is protected against antibiotic residues, antibiotic resistant genes and antibiotic resistant bacteria from the sewage treatment plant discharge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the discharge of treated municipal wastewater into rivers can be a source for antibiotic resistant bacteria and antibiotic residues.
the investigated river system is not a source of antibiotic resistance for the drinking water reservoir.
the investigated river system is a potential source for antibiotic resistance genes and resistant bacteria.
